title: SHINE: 4-month pediatric non-severe TB
dek: 2HRZ(E)/2HR for children and adolescents 3 months–16 years with non-severe DS-TB. Shorter because the lesion is smaller, not because kids are miniature Study 31.
story: SHINE showed that 4 months (2HRZ(E)/2HR) was non-inferior to 6 months for children with non-severe, presumed drug-susceptible TB. WHO made this a strong recommendation for ages 3 months to 16 years when disease is non-severe and MDR/RR is not suspected.

Non-severe is a defined clinical/radiographic object: limited smear-negative (or paucibacillary) pulmonary disease, peripheral lymph-node TB, no severe forms (miliary, TBM, osteoarticular, cavitary extensive). If you have to argue hard about “non-severe,” it is not SHINE.
This is not HPMZ. No rifapentine, no moxifloxacin requirement. Child-friendly FDCs and higher mg/kg bands still apply. Severe pediatric TB stays on longer, and TBM has its own recipe.
deep: HIV-positive children were included with caveats; they still need ART clocks and sometimes longer treatment if disease is not non-severe.
Ethambutol in the intensive phase depends on HIV prevalence and extent of disease — the (E) in 2HRZ(E).
A 15-year-old with adult-type cavitation is not a SHINE case; they may be HPMZ-eligible if ≥12 and DS, or six-month HRZE.
Source-case DST is pediatric DST when the child’s own NAAT is negative.

visual.caption: Pediatric DS-TB forks on severity. SHINE is the non-severe 4-month path. Severe disease, TBM, and RR-TB leave this plate.

example.title: Hilar nodes, smear-negative, source RIF-S
example.setup: 4-year-old, household index Xpert RIF not detected, CXR hilar adenopathy, no cavitation, HIV-negative, smear-negative, stool Ultra MTB detected.

steps.title: Non-severe?
steps.body: Limited intra-thoracic disease without severe forms: SHINE-shaped.

steps.title: Treat 4 months 2HRZ(E)/2HR
steps.body: Child FDC, include EMB if your NTP’s HIV-prevalence rule says so.

steps.title: If the source later flips to RR
steps.body: Rebuild. Pediatric DST often is the adult’s genome.

example.takeaway: SHINE shortens non-severe childhood TB, not all childhood TB.

choices: Children 3 months–16 years with non-severe DS-TB and no MDR/RR suspicion
check.answer: Children 3 months–16 years with non-severe DS-TB and no MDR/RR suspicion
check.why: Severity and DST prior are the gates.

check.prompt: A 13-year-old, 48 kg, adult-type cavitary DS-TB is closest to:
choices: An adult-type regimen decision (6-month HRZE or HPMZ if eligible) — not SHINE
check.answer: An adult-type regimen decision (6-month HRZE or HPMZ if eligible) — not SHINE
check.why: Cavitation is not non-severe. Age ≥12 may open HPMZ.

check.prompt: On the SHINE flow map, a “yes” at RR suspected leads where?
check.figureHint: Bottom end node from the RR decision.
